notes:
Lead source: self-serve signup via Hosted API sandbox (trial credits).

Background:
- Founded 2021; small CS-focused SaaS building an omnichannel agent assist product.
- Spun up a sandbox last week to prototype model-driven reply suggestions + semantic search of KB.

Discovery call (2026-03-03, FF id ff_20260303_1204_microburst_demo):
- Attendees: CEO (A. Ramos), Eng lead (C. Kim), Jordan (AE) + Priya (SE). Short product demo.
- "We saw 429s during a burst test — not sure if it's trial quota or concurrency." — C. Kim
- They ran parallel synthetic tests hitting /v1/generate with 8 concurrent clients and observed intermittent 429 + 50ms latency spikes.
- Primary asks: how Redwood handles short traffic bursts, quota model, soft vs hard rate limits, and recommended retry/backoff patterns for client SDKs.

Requirements / constraints (customer stated):
- Workloads: mainly chat and doc-search; occasional bulk embedding jobs for nightly index updates.
- Target 95p latency: <300ms for chat median, peaky bursts tolerated up to 1s if degraded gracefully.
- Throughput: typical steady-state 10 req/s, burst to 120 req/s for short windows (a few minutes) during marketing campaigns.
- Cost sensitivity: high — wants to avoid large reserve commitments initially.
- Security: SOC2 desired, basic audit logs, retention controls. No VPC / on-prem requirement at this stage.

What tripped them in trial:
- Self-serve sandbox applied default per-minute quotas; their stress test exceeded the quota and started returning 429s. They retried aggressively which worsened perceived failure rate.
- Unclear headers in the sandbox responses (they expected X-RateLimit style headers).

Recommendations discussed (SE notes):
- Explain difference between per-minute quota and concurrency window; provide example calculations converting req/s to token budget and quota units.
- Suggest client-side exponential backoff with randomized jitter and a capped retry count for 429s. Provide code snippet (follow up).
- Offer guidance on burst allowances: short-term credits / token bucket approach; Redwood hosted supports short bursts by default but needs configurable burst policy for predictable behavior.
- Fallback strategy: automatic model fallback to smaller/cheaper variant under throttling to preserve 90% availability.
- Monitoring: show how to surface rate-limit hit metrics in Console (per-key 429s, quota consumption, peak concurrency).

Timeline / activities:
- 2026-02-22: Self-serve signup, first API calls from sandbox.
- 2026-02-25: Spike from synthetic test — observed 429s.
- 2026-03-03: Discovery call + live repro (fireflies ff_20260303_1204_microburst_demo).
- 2026-03-05: Email thread started by Jordan summarizing retry/backoff best practices (see thread-CAKE1234-microburst-inbound).
- 2026-03-09: Follow-up with initial quota proposal attached (drive:/Redwood/pitch/microburst_pricing_v1.pdf).

Open items / blockers:
- They need explicit numbers: default concurrency limit per key + burst window size.
- Wants an example token-budget worksheet to map user traffic to monthly spend.
- Wants to see Console demo showing rate-limit metrics (to present to CTO).

Sales cadence & plan:
- Short-term: help them stabilize sandbox tests so they can continue evaluation this month. Provide a quick config to raise per-minute quota for their trial API key and enable more transparent rate-limit headers.
- Medium-term: if evaluation looks good, convert to small pay-as-you-go plan (no reserved commit). Forecast: low ARR initially 1k-10k.

Suggested immediate next steps (AE/SE action items):
- Send concise one-pager: "How Redwood handles quotas, bursts, and 429s" (include header examples, retry pseudocode, token budget worksheet).
- Temporary trial quota bump + enable debug headers on their key (INF-5643 opened).
- Schedule 30m console walkthrough w/ Priya to show rate-limit dashboards (proposed week of 2026-03-15).

Quote from Eng lead: "We just want predictable behavior during flash traffic — either graceful degradation or a clear retry contract."

CRM shorthand notes:
- low-touch SMB; wants self-serve path to production.
- major blocker: rate-limits + docs/examples.
- SE to deliver code snippet + quota calc by 2026-03-12.
notes_summary: SMB inbound via self-serve. Trial hit 429s during burst tests; primary needs are clear quota numbers, client retry guidance, and short-term trial quota bump. Interested in Hosted API only, cost sensitive. Next: send rate-limit one-pager + schedule console demo.
